chapter: Russell and Armstrong years, Goodman and the road
title: Trouble with police in Jacksonville and the guns question
summary: He recalls a Jacksonville cop's taunt on the beach, and says no one carried guns.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Do you remember anything, I mean like when you were traveling, some bad encounter with any whites or something where they forced you out of the town or - any real bad time that you may have had like when some whites may have -
Oh, yeah. You mean having trouble with white people?

We went to - bus broke down before we finally made it in - one place was Jacksonville, Florida. We played out on the beach, you know like Atlantic Pier? So when we got ready to come home, packed up, we'd have to walk between the cops like this. So one hollered at me and said, 'Good night, nigger.' I said, 'Good night, sir.' I sure did. ( ? )
He was trying to be smart or something?
No, this was in Jacksonville, Florida.
You were with Fletcher Henderson's band?
Tell me - the guys in that band, did you all carry a gun? Did you carry a pistol?
No, it was Louis Armstrong's band?
Did you all carry any pistols?
I haven't seen the first pistol.
Did any of the other guys have any guns?
No, I didn't see any guns.
